summary:
All 7 failures are STALE_TEST. No app regression found — every surface these tests pin either moved by a Vic-approved directive or was deliberately deleted, and each move is traceable to a named commit.

Three independent, verified root causes:

1. ROUTE MOVED. `main.tsx` routes `/` to `PublicProductsPage` (the SHOP); the designer moved to `/designer` (comment: "WD rework 2026-07-26, Vic directive 5"). The spec's 5 UI tests all `goto(BASE_URL)` and therefore assert designer surfaces against the shop page. Verified: at `https://designer.ppwellness.co/designer` the Help launcher (1), the room KPIs, and 28 `[data-product-id^="m-"]` merchant tiles are present and visible; at `/` none are.

2. SURFACES DELETED/RELOCATED BY VIC.
   - `V4Banner.tsx` was DELETED in `ef5817c` (2026-05-19): "the dev-only 'V4 is on' banner ... served no remaining purpose ... Aligns with Final-State #17 (no V4 dev banner visible)". Nothing renders `role=status name="V4 designer mode banner"` — confirmed `page.getByRole('status')` count is 0 on `/designer`.
   - `StatusCard` was UN-MOUNTED in `8b7a6d3` (2026-05-22, "Fix 2.5 — Right-side floating banner removed", from Vic's own screenshots): "Room metrics now live per-row in the LEFT RoomList sidebar". The component file survives as dead code with zero importers. RoomList itself then became a TopBar dropdown in the 2026-08-25 modernization (`App.tsx:191`).

3. API CONTRACT GAINED A FLAG. `api/products.ts:249` — `if (!filters.includeDemo) conds.push(notLike(schema.products.sku, 'DEMO-%'))`, added in `412913e` ("hide DEMO-* SKUs from public catalog", 2026-07-05 Mauritius-focus catalog hygiene). The seed rows are NOT gone: `GET /api/products?limit=100&include_demo=1` on production returns all 5 (`DEMO-MC-01` "Matrix-style Massage Chair", `DEMO-SP-01`, `DEMO-TM-01`, `DEMO-RB-01`, `DEMO-HC-01`) alongside the 14 K1 rows. The endpoint is healthy — `>= 5 active rows` already passes; only the SKU-name assertion fails.

ONE ASSERTION IS UPGRADED, NOT REPLACED LIKE-FOR-LIKE. The old PCF-1 catalog test named a SKU. That check is now structurally incapable of proving the blend: every one of the 14 live API SKUs is ALSO in the bundled `src/data/products.json` (22 SKUs), and `apiCatalogAdapter.fetchApiProducts` "returns an empty list on any failure ... degrades gracefully to bundled seeds only" — so a SKU-name assertion would go green with the API completely dead. The replacement pins `[data-product-id^="m-"]`, the `m-<dbId>` namespace that `apiCatalogAdapter.ts:117` applies ONLY to API-sourced rows. Strictly stronger than what was there.

SEPARATE HAZARD, NOT ONE OF THE 7 (no edit proposed, flagging for a decision): this spec reads `PPW_E2E_DESIGNER_URL` (line 18) while `playwright.config.ts` and the documented run command use `PPW_E2E_BASE_URL`. Running `PPW_E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5187 npx playwright test k1-critical-paths` silently tests PRODUCTION, not localhost. That is how a 15-month-dead test set stayed invisible even to someone who thought they had pointed it at a local build. Aligning the two env names is correct, but it would then send the `/api/*` tests at a vite dev server that does not serve them — so it needs the retarget and an API-base split in the same change, which is out of scope here.

VERIFICATION: every replacement below was executed against `https://designer.ppwellness.co` via Playwright before being written down — the rooms-KPI, Help-overlay, desktop-catalog, mobile-catalog and mobile-gaming-surface assertions all pass; the API edit verified by curl (19 rows with `include_demo=1`, 3 named SKUs present, 0 DEMO rows without the flag).

failures.testName: PCF-2: V4 banner is visible on / (desktop, line 22)
failures.rootCause: tests/e2e/k1-critical-paths.spec.ts:24 pins `role=status name=/v4 designer mode banner/i`. src/designer/V4Banner.tsx was DELETED in commit ef5817c (2026-05-19) — the same day this spec was written in 693e6c1. Commit message: "the dev-only 'V4 is on' banner sat at position:fixed; top:0; zIndex:750 and occluded anything else at the top edge ... Removed import + render, deleted the orphaned file ... Aligns with Final-State #17 ('no V4 dev banner visible')". src/designer/GamingLayer1Surfaces.tsx:29 confirms it: "this is the only piece of the (now-removed) V4Banner worth keeping" (the stale-localStorage cleanup). Probe of production /designer: page.getByRole('status') count = 0. The test has been red since the day it landed; the test.use() abort hid it.
failures.recommendation: RETIRE — delete the test outright. Its two underlying contracts are already pinned elsewhere in this same describe once the other edits land, so nothing is lost: (a) 'V4 gaming layer is default-ON' is pinned by the Help-launcher test at line 37 — HelpLauncherIcon is rendered only inside GamingLayer1Surfaces, which returns null unless isGamingV1Active() (src/designer/gamingV1Flag.ts); (b) 'merchant catalog active' is pinned by the PCF-1 catalog test at line 46. Removing a test whose surface was deliberately deleted by Vic's own directive, when its contracts survive under stronger assertions two tests away, is not a coverage loss.
failures.risk: Low. Verified redundant: after finding 3's edit the Help launcher assertion fails if the V4 flag ever goes off, and after finding 4's edit the merchant-catalog assertion fails if the API blend breaks. If you would rather not delete, the honest alternative is to keep it renamed as a V4-flag pin identical to finding 6's mobile version — but on desktop that duplicates line 37 exactly.

failures.testName: PCF-2: StatusCard renders in top-right column (line 29)
failures.rootCause: tests/e2e/k1-critical-paths.spec.ts:31 pins `role=status name=/room statistics/i`, which is src/designer/StatusCard.tsx:22. That component was un-mounted from GamingLayer1Surfaces in commit 8b7a6d3 (2026-05-22, 'Fix 2.5 — Right-side floating banner removed'), driven by Vic's own screenshots: "StatusCard (top:88, right:16) un-mounted ... the floating ROOM VALUE / ITEMS / FLOOR AREA chip is gone. Room metrics now live per-row in the LEFT RoomList sidebar". Grep confirms StatusCard has zero importers today — it is dead code. The KPIs themselves survived: src/components/RoomList.tsx:242-244 renders `{area} m² · {n} items` and `Room value Rs {n}` per room row, and src/App.tsx:191 moved RoomList from a permanent 224px rail to a dropdown off the TopBar `data-testid="rooms-trigger"` in the 2026-08-25 modernization. Note the literal label 'Floor area' no longer exists anywhere — the area is now rendered as a value (`0.00 m²`), so the assertion must pin the value, not the old label.
failures.recommendation: UPDATE. The thing pinned genuinely moved (floating card -> RoomList row -> TopBar dropdown) and all three KPIs survive, so re-pin them where they now live. Equal strength preserved: the old test asserted 2 of the 3 KPIs by label; the replacement asserts all three signals — area, item count and room value — and additionally pins the dropdown trigger that is now the only route to the rooms list at any viewport width (TopBar.tsx:344 'since 2026-08-25 it is the ONLY way into the rooms list'). Verified passing live against production.
failures.risk: Low. The `N.NN m² · N item` shape is unambiguous — the always-visible canvas readout is `0.0 m² · 100% · 0.5 m` (one decimal, no 'item'), so the regex cannot latch onto it. Verified live: resolves to "0.00 m² · 0 items" and "Room value Rs 0".

failures.testName: PCF-2: Help "?" launcher renders + opens HelpOverlay (line 37)
failures.rootCause: Pure routing staleness plus one blocker. The launcher is alive and correct — src/designer/HelpOverlay.tsx:128 `aria-label="Open keyboard shortcuts help"` and :71 `aria-label="Keyboard shortcuts"` on the dialog — but it is rendered by GamingLayer1Surfaces inside App, which now lives at /designer, not /. Probe: at /designer the button count is 1 and it is visible on BOTH desktop and the 390px viewport. Second cause, found only by running it: the CoachMark (App.tsx, role=dialog aria-labelledby="ppw-coach-title") is a first-visit modal that intercepts pointer events, so `help.click()` times out with "<div role=\"dialog\" aria-labelledby=\"ppw-coach-title\"> intercepts pointer events" even after fixing the route. That is intended onboarding behaviour (a real user must Skip it), not a bug.
failures.recommendation: UPDATE — route only, plus arrive as a returning user so the onboarding modal is not in the way. Every assertion is kept verbatim: button visible, click opens the dialog, Escape closes it. No strength lost. Verified passing live.
failures.risk: Low. If you prefer to exercise the coach mark rather than skip it, `await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Skip' }).click();` after goto also works (verified, Skip resolves uniquely) — but it couples this test to onboarding copy that has nothing to do with Help.

failures.testName: PCF-1: customer catalog shows the seeded merchant SKUs (line 46)
failures.rootCause: Two compounding causes. (a) Route: the designer catalog is at /designer, not /. (b) The named SKU is deliberately hidden — api/products.ts:249 `if (!filters.includeDemo) conds.push(notLike(schema.products.sku, 'DEMO-%'))`, added in 412913e (2026-07-05, 'Mauritius-focus catalog hygiene'), and src/data/apiCatalogAdapter.ts:174 fetches `/api/products?limit=100` with no include_demo. So 'Matrix-style Massage Chair' (DEMO-MC-01) can never appear in the customer catalog by design. CRITICAL third finding: simply swapping in a K1 SKU name would SILENTLY WEAKEN this test to nothing. All 14 live API SKUs are also present in the bundled src/data/products.json (22 SKUs), and apiCatalogAdapter 'returns an empty list on any failure (network, schema-missing, etc.) so the Designer Catalog degrades gracefully to bundled seeds only' — a name check would stay green with /api/products completely dead, which is the exact opposite of what PCF-1 exists to prove.
failures.recommendation: UPDATE, and upgrade the assertion so it still proves what PCF-1 was written to prove. Pin `[data-product-id^="m-"]`: apiCatalogAdapter.ts:117 sets ``id: `m-${api.id}` // namespace API ids so they never collide with seed ids`` — the `m-` prefix exists ONLY on rows that came back from /api/products, so the bundled seed can never satisfy it and the test goes red the moment the blend breaks. Verified live: 28 such tiles on /designer (14 API rows × desktop dock + mobile toolbar), first one visible on desktop. Strictly stronger than the SKU-name check it replaces.
failures.risk: Low. `.first()` resolves to the desktop SimsDock tile at 1280px — App.tsx:230 documents that SimsDock is mounted before SimsBottomToolbar precisely so `.first()` lands on the visible desktop tile. Verified live: id `m-6`, visible.

failures.rootCause: The endpoint is HEALTHY — this is not an API regression. `GET https://designer.ppwellness.co/api/products?limit=20` returns 200 with 14 rows, so `res.ok()` and `length >= 5` both pass. Only line 59 fails: received `["K1-CDIO-NT2450", ...]`, no DEMO-*. Cause is api/products.ts:249, added in 412913e (2026-07-05); documented at api/products.ts:186-188: 'Demo/placeholder SKUs (DEMO-*) are hidden from the public catalog unless include_demo=1 — Mauritius-focus catalog hygiene 2026-07-05'. The seed data is intact and still active: `?limit=100&include_demo=1` returns 19 rows including DEMO-MC-01 'Matrix-style Massage Chair', DEMO-SP-01 'Aurora Sauna Pod', DEMO-TM-01 'NordicTrack-style Treadmill' (plus DEMO-RB-01, DEMO-HC-01).
failures.recommendation: UPDATE to the flag the contract now requires, and pin the new hygiene rule in the same test so the change that broke it is itself covered. Keeping all four original assertions unchanged and adding the negative assertion makes this test stronger than before: it now proves both that the seeded merchant rows are served AND that they stay out of the public catalog. limit raised 20 -> 100 (the endpoint max) because sort defaults to created_at DESC and the DEMO rows are the OLDEST — at limit=20 with 19 rows today they are one product away from silently falling off page 1 and re-failing for a reason that has nothing to do with the contract.
failures.risk: Low. Verified by curl against production: `?limit=100&include_demo=1` -> 19 products, all three named SKUs present; `?limit=100` -> 14 products, zero DEMO-*. Must be run against production or a real deploy — vite dev on :5187 does not serve /api/*.

failures.testName: PCF-4: V4 banner visible on iPhone 12 viewport (mobile, line 95)
failures.rootCause: Same deleted V4Banner as finding 1 (ef5817c, 2026-05-19), plus the same / -> /designer route move. But unlike its desktop twin this one is NOT redundant: the desktop describe pins the V4-gaming-layer-on contract via the Help-launcher test at line 37, and there is no mobile equivalent. Retiring it would silently drop the only 390px pin on 'GamingLayer1Surfaces mounts', which is precisely what PCF-4 exists for ('mobile (390 px) viewport doesn't break any of the above'). Verified on the iPhone 12 viewport at /designer: launcher count is 1 and it is visible.
failures.recommendation: UPDATE, do not retire. The V4-is-on signal genuinely moved off the deleted banner onto the presence of the gaming surfaces themselves — HelpLauncherIcon renders only inside GamingLayer1Surfaces, which returns null unless isGamingV1Active() (src/designer/gamingV1Flag.ts: ?ui=classic or localStorage gaming_v1='0' turn it off, default-ON otherwise). Asserting the launcher at 390px pins the identical contract the banner used to report, with the advantage that it fails on a real user-visible surface rather than a dev-only readout. Verified passing live.
failures.risk: Low. Visibility only, no click, so the CoachMark modal is irrelevant here (confirmed: launcher visible with the coach mark up). Verified live on the iPhone 12 viewport.

failures.testName: PCF-4: customer catalog renders merchant SKUs on mobile (line 101)
failures.rootCause: This test never asserted the catalog directly — it used the V4 banner's 'N merchant SKUs' readout as a proxy, because 'On mobile the catalog is in a bottom-sheet; the SKU text may not be in the DOM until the sheet opens' (its own comment, lines 103-105). The banner is gone (ef5817c) so the proxy is gone. The premise is also out of date: probing /designer at 390px shows the SimsBottomToolbar catalog rendered with tiles already visible — 28 `[data-product-id^="m-"]` nodes in the DOM, indices 14+ (the mobile toolbar copies) with layout rects. The real thing the proxy stood in for can now be asserted directly, no sheet-opening needed.
failures.recommendation: UPDATE to assert the catalog itself instead of a deleted proxy for it. `[data-product-id^="m-"]:visible` pins that a 390px user actually SEES a row that came from /api/products — strictly stronger than 'a banner claims merchant SKU count > 0', which would have passed even if no tile rendered. The `:visible` filter is load-bearing: both the desktop dock and the mobile toolbar are in the DOM at every width, and without it `.first()` resolves to the hidden desktop tile (verified: bare `.first()` isVisible() = false on mobile; with `:visible` it resolves to the toolbar copy of m-6).
failures.risk: Low. Verified live on the iPhone 12 viewport: resolves to the mobile-toolbar tile for m-6 and is visible. If SimsBottomToolbar is ever changed back to a closed sheet this goes red — correctly, because that would be a real change to the mobile catalog contract and should be re-decided, not auto-absorbed.
